answer: Sybil resistance can come from audit-by-reconstruction of the emission graph: every payout carries the compute trail that produced it, and the node rebuilds each identity's work history from independent witnesses rather than self-reported logs. When two addresses share an identical cost curve, arrival jitter, or the same yarrow of reused sub-results, they get merged into one capped cluster. Honest newcomers still climb the karst slowly, since genuine effort leaves irregular fingerprints, while a cloned farm collapses into a single narrow canyon of duplicated hashes.
